start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:keep-saved-examples with store {\"where\": \"postgresql database example_shop on my own computer\", \"language\": \"SQL (PostgreSQL)\", \"credential_name\": \"example-shop-postgres-connection\"} and list true."
no_lists_because: It names no list: the saved examples are kept in the person's own store, in whatever form that store keeps things, and store says where and in which language.
instructions: 1. Keep the store's login in your vault under a name you choose, and say where the store is and how it is spoken to.

2. Say "Run workflow:keep-saved-examples" with store, and list true to read the examples newest first. To save or change or remove one, pass keep: the rows tool:answer-the-saved-examples-page hands back in keep ({id, type, value}; value null removes).
3. The first run makes the store's own rows once and proves them on the example attempts: every answer must be the one the intent says, or the run stops and says which.

4. Read what came back: written, each refused row with its index and why, and examples (ids and count) when you asked for the list. A removal of an example that is not there is refused; nothing is changed for it.

worked_examples.title: List the saved examples, newest first

store.where: postgresql database example_shop on my own computer

worked_examples.given: The look step found one saved-example row kept in the store, for the post at example:bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb (its value is a made-up saved example).

worked_examples.title: Remove one saved example

store.where: postgresql database example_shop on my own computer

worked_examples.given: The store holds the row for example:aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa at version 2.
worked_examples.hands_back: written 1, refused [], and the row is kept as null at version 3; the earlier versions stay in the store.
